(Japanese: '''ステップ・バイ・ステップ！ドット＆ウェルカモ！！''' ''Step by Step! Dot and {{tt|Welkamo|Quaxwell}}!!'') is the 128th episode of ''[[Pokémon Horizons: The Series]]'', and the 1,360th episode of the [[Pokémon animated series]]. It first aired in Japan on February 20, 2026<!-- and is scheduled to air in the United States on *day*-->.

==Plot==
While having food made by [[Murdock]] in their hotel room, [[Roy]] proposes visiting the [[Black Rayquaza]] at the [[Dragon's Den]] since not only is it an important part of their search of Pokémon with eighteen {{Tera}} [[type]]s, but there is also [[Friede]]'s [[HZ122|briefcase that is meant for]] the {{pkmn|category|Sky High Pokémon}}. [[Liko]] and [[Ult]] agree to the idea, but the former is still worried about [[Dot]]'s [[HZ127|situation]]. Elsewhere, {{an|Iono}} is also feeling conflicted about Dot when she spots {{p|Quaxwell}} training with {{TP|Dot|Tinkaton}} and {{TP|Dot|Gholdengo}}. Watching them train together, she gets an idea while recording them on her [[Rotom Phone]]. Later, Ult calls out Dot for backing out as a {{pkmn|Trainer}}, though Liko and Roy know he just wants to see Rayquaza as soon as possible. While Ult is brash with his words, Iono agrees Dot cannot {{pkmn|battle}} alongside her friends as she arrives to their room. The [[Levincia]] [[Gym Leader]] asks Dot if she truly understands her partner while showing the footage she recorded earlier. Iono then provokes Dot into a battle to prove the latter understands Quaxwell as well as she claims. 

Everyone moves to an open area where the rest of the [[Rising Volt Tacklers]] also spectate. {{p|Bellibolt}} makes the first move by charging up electricity, but contrary to Dot's expectations for either {{m|Spark}} or {{m|Discharge}}, it instead uses {{m|Thunder}}. Quaxwell avoids all the lightning strikes that come from the attack and attacks with {{m|Aqua Cutter}}, but Bellibolt not only jumps out of the way throughout the barrage, it also charges up electricity in the process. Again contrary to Dot's expectations for a {{type|Electric}} [[move]], Iono has Bellibolt use {{m|Mud Shot}}, which successfully hits Quaxwell despite his attempts to cut through it with Aqua Cutter, reducing his {{stat|speed}} and leaving him more vulnerable to the EleFrog Pokémon's Thunder. As a result of his reduced speed and stepping into a puddle of water made by Aqua Cutter earlier, Quaxwell is struck by a {{DL|Type|Type effectiveness|supereffective}} Thunder and takes severe [[damage]]. Dot begins to lose her confidence again and Iono points out the Dot she knows has always continued battling even when things get tough before questioning if she forgot something important. 

Looking at Quaxwell, Dot realizes what she was lacking and decides to press on. Iono is pleased to see Dot gaining some spark of her determined self back, so she has her partner use Thunder again. This time, Dot has Quaxwell use the water puddles to make up for its reduced speed after remembering what she saw from Iono's recording, allowing him to not only dodge all the lightning strikes, but also get close enough to land a {{m|Liquidation}} attack. However, this triggers its {{a|Electromorphosis}} [[Ability]], generating even more electricity. Rather than use an Electric-type move, Iono catches everyone off guard when she calls for Bellibolt to use {{m|Slack Off}} instead. When she sees Quaxwell moving while Bellibolt was healing itself, Dot has an idea. Both Dot and Quaxwell pull back their hair and coif respectively, ready to battle harder as Bellibolt unleashes Thunder that is stronger than before. Nonetheless, Quaxwell runs through it all despite the risk of a lightning strike hitting a puddle. Dot encourages her partner to run faster as she recalls the times they overcame things together, with Quaxwell forming a wave as he runs. Just as Bellibolt runs out of electricity, resulting in Thunder being cleared up, Dot commands Quaxwell use {{m|Wave Crash}} with the wave he made, mimicking Tinkaton and Gholdengo's movements in the process. After landing, Quaxwell glows in a blue light, [[Evolution|evolving]] into {{TP|Dot|Quaquaval}}, making Dot happy.

In response to this, Iono pulls out her [[Tera Orb]] and Terastallizes Bellibolt, with Dot doing the same with her newly evolved Quaquaval, Terastallizing into a pure {{t|Water}} type. A smokescreen made by a clash between Mud Shot and Aqua Cutter allows Quaquaval to run up to Bellibolt and kick it into the air with {{m|Low Kick}}. Bellibolt uses Thunder again, but Quaquaval is able to cancel it out before running up to the EleFrog Pokémon. Iono's plan for an unexpected {{m|Sucker Punch}} backfires when Dot remembers how Iono likes to [[HZ050|overreact whenever she is hiding something]]. Quaquaval finishes off Bellibolt with another Wave Crash and the Levincia Gym Leader accepts her defeat. Dot compliments her partner as Iono comes up to her, happy to see her confidence restored. Dot walks up to her friends and, with the Dancer Pokémon's encouragement, asks to join as a Trainer for one of the eighteen Tera types again, which they happily accept.

Later that night, the group including Iono have a celebration feast, where Iono pulls Dot into a dance after seeing the Pokémon having fun. Afterwards, Dot stays behind in [[Paldea]] with the others to continue with her analysis while Liko, Roy, and Ult head off to the Dragon's Den to see Rayquaza again.

==Major events==
<!-- This is not for summarizing everything that happens in this episode. Only events pertaining to the series as a whole, such as catching and releasing Pokémon and obtaining Badges, go here. -->
* [[Dot]]'s {{p|Quaxwell}} learns {{m|Wave Crash}} and [[Evolution|evolves]] into {{TP|Dot|Quaquaval}}.
* Dot has a [[rematch]] against {{an|Iono}} and wins.
* [[Liko]], [[Roy]], and [[Ult]] set off for the [[Dragon's Den]] to deliver [[Friede]]'s [[HZ122|gift]] to the [[Black Rayquaza]].

==Trivia==
[[File:Pokémon Horizons 30th Anniversary artwork.jpg|250px|thumb|right|{{aniseries|HZ}} promotional artwork for Pokémon's 30th Anniversary]]
* [[Mega Nidothing's Mega Mega! Mega Evolution]]: {{p|Pinsir}}
* The first [[List of Pokémon Horizons: The Series eyecatches|eyecatch]] features [[Iono]] and her {{p|Bellibolt}} and the second features [[Dot]] with her {{TP|Dot|Quaxwell}}, {{TP|Dot|Tinkaton}}, and {{TP|Dot|Gholdengo}}.
* This episode marks the first time in all of the {{pkmn|animated series}} that all of the concurrent [[first partner Pokémon]] have reached their final stage of [[Evolution]].
* As of this episode:
** All of the Pokémon owned by the younger members of the [[Rising Volt Tacklers]] are fully evolved.
** All of the evolved forms of the [[Paldea first partner Pokémon]] have appeared in the animated series.
** [[Pagogo]] is the only single-type Pokémon owned by the younger members of the Rising Volt Tacklers.
* Artwork of [[Liko]], [[Roy]], Dot, [[Ult]] and their Pokémon was released after this episode to commemorate [[Pokémon 30th Anniversary|Pokémon's 30th Anniversary]], also being released as a [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xWKvPxNBruw/ motion poster with a promotional video] for the next episode.
* Roy, Ult, {{p|Sableye}}, Pagogo, and Liko narrate the preview for the [[HZ129|next episode]].

===Errors===
* Dot's Quaxwell uses {{m|Wave Crash}} in this episode, despite {{p|Quaxwell}} being [[Animated series move errors|unable to learn the move]] in the {{pkmn|games}} without evolving into {{p|Quaquaval}} first. This marks the first instance of an animated series move error in {{aniseries|HZ}}.
